subject: Re: Atlasium Labs — SDK shim, tracing and security vetting
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@atlasium.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@atlasium.ai>
Date: 2025-05-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: Atlasium SDK shim + tracing — quick sync request

Hi Neha —

Thanks again for the call last week. Atlasium built a small compatibility shim to let our customers use the Atlasium SDK as a drop-in for LangChain / LlamaIndex stacks while preserving token-level tracing and attribution. We heard from three mutual beta customers that being able to surface Redwood trace ids inside their toolchains is a requirement for SRE and billing reconciliation.

We want to run this by Redwood product/security to validate the approach (no data exfiltration, KMS compatibility, and how the shim propagates Redwood request ids). Attached is a short architecture sketch and a draft SOW (atlasium-sdk-architecture.pdf, Atlasium-Redwood-SOW-v0.3.docx).

Requested: a 30-min technical review with whoever owns SDK partnerships + our security engineering lead. Are you available Tue/Wed next week?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Partnerships — Atlasium Labs
samira@atlasium.ai

Attachments: atlasium-sdk-architecture.pdf (pdf), Atlasium-Redwood-SOW-v0.3.docx (docx)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Samira —

Appreciate the deck and SOW. We can do a quick technical review. Vanessa (partnerships lead) and Karthik (runtime integrations) are cc'd — they’ll triage the security and compatibility items.

High-level asks from our side for the review:
- A brief demo of the shim in a LangChain flow (how you instrument calls, where Redwood ids are injected).
- TLS/KMS flow: do you require customer-managed keys or use your own?
- Data residency and whether the shim buffers any request payloads off-network.
- Any changes to user prompt content or tokenization before reach Redwood.

I can do Wed 2025-05-21 16:00 UTC or Thu 2025-05-22 09:00 UTC. Which works?

Neha Kapoor

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-16T12:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Atlasium SDK shim + tracing — quick sync request

Thanks Samira — forwarding to Karthik for runtime review. Two quick internal notes for Neha:
- We should confirm that Atlasium’s shim keeps Redwood request ids immutable and makes no secondary backchannel calls. If there are any local caches, ensure they are encrypted and TTL-limited.
- If they want an official "Redwood verified" badge for the integration, we'll need a conformance checklist (instrumentation test harness) and a short performance benchmark for cold/hot KV cache behavior.

Karthik, can you validate if the architecture sketch aligns with our kernel selection and KV cache expectations? If not, flag areas where the shim could cause latency/regression.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@atlasium.ai>

On Fri, May 16, 2025 at 12:18 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Samira — forwarding to Karthik for runtime review. Two quick internal notes for Neha:
> - We should confirm that Atlasium’s shim keeps Redwood request ids immutable and makes no secondary backchannel calls. If there are any local caches, ensure they are encrypted and TTL-limited.
> - If they want an official "Redwood verified" badge for the integration, we'll need a conformance checklist (instrumentation test harness) and a short performance benchmark for cold/hot KV cache behavior.

Thanks Vanessa — a couple clarifications from our engineering team:
- The shim attaches a header X-Redwood-Trace and echoes the request id from the client when present. It does not open separate telemetry channels to Atlasium backend; we delegated telemetry to the host app by default.
- We do have an optional local cache (configurable). By default it’s disabled; when enabled it uses AES-256 + customer-specific salt. TTL defaults to 5 minutes.

We’ll prepare a short sandbox demo that shows the header propagation and artifact-free tracing. Can we book Wed 2025-05-21 16:00 UTC as Neha suggested? That slot works for Jordan (engineering) and Samira.

— Jordan Reed
Platform Engineer | Atlasium Labs
jordan.reed@atlasium.ai
